One hour after Tanya left, Jose started bicycling along the same road from school to the park. Tanya ran at a constant rate of $2$ miles per hour faster than Patrick walked, Jose bicycled at a constant rate of $7$ miles per hour faster than Tanya ran, and all three arrived at the park at the same time. Step 3:  We know that the distance from school to the park is the same for all three, and they all arrive at the park at the same time.
Step 4:  We can use the formula $distance = speed \times time$ to express the distance traveled by each person in terms of their speed and the time taken.
Step 5:  For Patrick, the distance traveled is $pt$, where $t$ is the time taken by Patrick to reach the park. Since Tanya starts running one hour after Patrick, the time taken by Tanya is $t-1$.
Step 6:  Similarly, for Jose, the distance traveled is $(p+9)(t-2)$, as he starts two hours after Patrick and Tanya.
Step 7:  Equating the distances traveled by Patrick, Tanya, and Jose, we get the equation $pt = (p+2)(t-1) = (p+9)(t-2)$.
Step 8:  Solving this equation will give us the value of $t$ in terms of $p$.
Step 9:  Once we have the value of $t$, we can use it to find the distance from school to the park by substituting it back into the equation $pt$.
